title: Internal scalar-extension flatness tested on sectionwise module sheaves
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site small in a coefficient universe $w$. Assume abelian sheafification exists, its local equivalences are monoidal, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab})$ has the closed symmetric monoidal structure of sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects in $\mathcal A$, and let $R_{\mathrm{sec}},S_{\mathrm{sec}}$ and $\varphi_{\mathrm{sec}}$ be their reconstructed section-ring sheaves and ring-sheaf map. Write $E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\mathrm{sec}})$ and $E_S:\operatorname{Mod}_S(\mathcal A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(S_{\mathrm{sec}})$ for the underlying-abelian-sheaf preserving equivalences [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Let $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ be internal extension and restriction of scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Give $S_{\mathrm{sec}}$ its $R_{\mathrm{sec}}$-module structure through $\varphi_{\mathrm{sec}}$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$E_R\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(M)\ \cong\ S_{\mathrm{sec}}\otimes_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}E_R(M)$$
with sheafified sectionwise tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], characterized on local pure tensors by $s\otimes m\mapsto s\otimes m$. For $u:M\to N$ it intertwines the induced map on the left with $1\otimes E_R(u)$. Moreover $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$ preserves finite limits if and only if $S_{\mathrm{sec}}$ is a flat $R_{\mathrm{sec}}$-module sheaf [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. All rings and module section groups lie in $w$.

proof.text: Write $A=R_{\mathrm{sec}}$, $B=S_{\mathrm{sec}}$, and $V:\operatorname{Mod}(B)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ for sectionwise restriction. The equivalences $E_R,E_S$ preserve underlying sheaves and section maps. The internal restricted action evaluates to $r\cdot n=\varphi_{\mathrm{sec}}(r)n$, exactly the action defining $V$. Thus the identity on sections gives $E_R\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\cong VE_S$, naturally in the module. Put $Q(F)=(U\mapsto B(U)\otimes_{A(U)}F(U))^\#$, with $B$ acting on the first factor, and $Q(f)$ induced by $s\otimes m\mapsto s\otimes f(m)$. This is the sheaf change-of-rings construction; the identity and composition laws hold on pure tensors and hence after sheafification.

source.place: Sections 03CS and 03CX: restriction and sheafified change of rings; definition of the section action in the cited internal-module equivalence.

proof.text: For an $A$-module sheaf $F$ and a $B$-module sheaf $N$, a map $h:F\to VN$ induces $B(U)\otimes_{A(U)}F(U)\to N(U)$ by $s\otimes m\mapsto s h_U(m)$. It is balanced since $s\varphi(r)h_U(m)=s h_U(rm)$, is $B(U)$-linear, and commutes with restriction since $h$ and the actions do. The module-sheafification universal property extends it uniquely to $QF\to N$. Conversely evaluate a map $g:QF\to N$ on $1\otimes m$. The two constructions are inverse: $h(m)$ is recovered from $1h(m)$, and $g(s\otimes m)=s g(1\otimes m)$. Both commute with precomposition in $F$ and postcomposition in $N$. Consequently $Q\dashv V$, with unit $j_F(m)=[1\otimes m]$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict: write out the two inverse maps using the balanced tensor and Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules.

proof.text: The closed sheaf tensor preserves colimits in either variable, so the hypotheses of the internal extension-restriction adjunction hold. Its unit $u_M$ is insertion of the unit of $S$ followed by the coequalizer map. Transport this adjunction through $E_R,E_S$, inserting their unit and counit isomorphisms; step 1 identifies its right adjoint with $V$. Uniqueness of left adjoints, in its unit-compatible form, therefore gives a natural $B$-linear isomorphism $c_M:E_S\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(E_RM)$ satisfying $V(c_M)E_R(u_M)=j_{E_RM}$, under the restriction identification. Thus $c_M([1\otimes m])=[1\otimes m]$. In the internal coequalizer the $S$-action is on the first factor, so $[s\otimes m]=s[1\otimes m]$; $B$-linearity gives $c_M([s\otimes m])=[s\otimes m]$. This fixes the direction and normalization of the comparison, rather than merely identifying its two objects.

source.place: Internal adjunction and unit: cited blueprint definition; comparison: Tag 0B65, categories-lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, applied after the elementary Hom-set transport.

proof.text: As an $A$-module sheaf, $VQ(F)$ is $T(F)=B\otimes_A F$. Indeed both are the abelian sheafification of the identical presheaf $U\mapsto B(U)\otimes_{A(U)}F(U)$; the restricted $A$-action in both constructions is the unique extension of $r(s\otimes m)=\varphi(r)s\otimes m=s\otimes rm$. Hence the identity on presheaf tensors extends to a natural $A$-linear isomorphism $VQ\cong T$. Compose this with $V(c_M)$ and the step-1 restriction identification to obtain the asserted $\theta_M:E_R\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(M)\cong T(E_RM)$. Its pure-tensor formula follows from step 3. For $u:M\to N$, naturality of $c$ gives $\theta_N E_R\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(u)=T(E_Ru)\theta_M$, where $T(E_Ru)=1\otimes E_Ru$ by the defining tensor map. Equality is tested on presheaf pure tensors using tensor generation and the uniqueness in sheafification.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, and Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules: the two module structures extend the same presheaf action.

proof.text: The categories $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ have finite limits computed sectionwise, with the same underlying abelian-sheaf limits. Since $V$ changes only scalar action, the $A$-action on the limit of $VN_j$ is the restriction of the coordinatewise $B$-action on the limit of $N_j$. Thus $V$ preserves finite limits, including the empty one. It also reflects isomorphisms: if a $B$-linear map $f$ has inverse $g$ as an $A$-linear sheaf map, then on sections $f(g(sn))=sn=f(sg(n))$, so $g(sn)=sg(n)$, and $g$ is $B$-linear. Apply the conservative left-exact reflection criterion to conclude that $V$ reflects finite limits.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits; reflection of finite limits is the cited generic categorical criterion.

proof.text: Equivalences and their quasi-inverses preserve limits; their unit and counit isomorphisms and invariance under natural isomorphism show that $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$ preserves finite limits if and only if $Q$ does, using $E_S\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\cong QE_R$ from step 3. Explicitly, a diagram of $A$-module sheaves can be pulled back along the quasi-inverse of $E_R$ and returned along its counit; the same applies to cones, so no restriction to diagrams already presented as $E_R$-images is imposed. If $Q$ preserves finite limits, so does $VQ$ by step 5, and hence so does $T$ by step 4. Conversely, if $T$ preserves finite limits, the natural isomorphism $VQ\cong T$ gives finite-limit preservation of $VQ$; cancel the reflecting functor $V$ by the finite-limit cancellation lemma to get preservation by $Q$. This proves $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$ preserves finite limits if and only if $T$ does.

source.place: Tag 0038, categories-lemma-adjoint-exact, for equivalences; natural-isomorphism invariance and reflection cancellation are the two cited categorical tools.

proof.text: The sheaf tensor result makes $T=B\otimes_A-$ a left adjoint, and therefore $T$ preserves finite colimits. Its symmetry isomorphism $B\otimes_A F\cong F\otimes_A B$, induced by $s\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes s$, is natural in $F$. Thus the right-exact functor in the definition of flatness is isomorphic to $T$. By the definition of exactness as preservation of finite limits and finite colimits, $B$ is a flat $A$-module sheaf if and only if $T$ preserves finite limits. Combine this with step 6. All tensor factors and section modules used above lie in $w$; only finite diagrams are used for the exactness test, so the stipulated small-site and coefficient-universe hypotheses suffice.
